title: Amazon Mining Watch's convolutional-network detector maps gold-mining scars basin-wide; 496,000 ha of protected and Indigenous lands affected 2018-2025, with no documented enforcement action
summary: AI mining detector (Earth Genome, Amazon Conservation, Pulitzer Center) maps mining scars basin-wide; 496,000 ha in protected areas 2018-2025 reported Apr 2026; no attributable enforcement event.
account: Amazon Mining Watch is a public platform built by the Pulitzer Center's Rainforest Investigations Network, Amazon Conservation Association and Earth Genome that, in its own words, leverages artificial intelligence to map the impact of gold mining. Its code repository describes the detector as an ensemble of convolutional neural networks trained on hand-labeled Sentinel-2 patches, run over the 8.2 million km2 Amazon basin, with detections recomputed yearly for 2018-2025 and quarterly from 2025; the repository reports specificity 0.976 and sensitivity 0.991 on a Venezuelan geographic holdout for the cumulative 2024 detections. Mongabay reported on 24 April 2026 (the publication date used here as date observed) that the platform's quarterly report found about 6,000 hectares of mining deforestation in protected areas and Indigenous territories in the last three months of 2025 and 496,000 hectares affected between 2018 and 2025. The enforcement operations the earlier verifier examined are documented by the same tool maker without any AI role: MAAP #104 (4 August 2019) attributes a 92% fall in gold-mining deforestation at La Pampa to Peru's Operation Mercury of February 2019 using satellite imagery (ESA, Maxar, Sentinel-1) with no mention of machine learning. No fetched source documents an enforcement action taken on an Amazon Mining Watch detection, so the record is a general benefit without an attributable event.
purpose: Automated detection and mapping of artisanal gold-mining scars in satellite imagery for journalists, researchers, civil society and policymakers; the mapping is the intended use.
system: Amazon Mining Watch gold-mine detector (ensemble of convolutional neural networks on Sentinel-2 imagery)
model_version: 48px_v4.10b-18d-20g-21a-22bc-ensemble (July 2026 production model, per the repository README)
developer: Earth Genome (model), with Amazon Conservation Association and the Pulitzer Center's Rainforest Investigations Network
deployer: Amazon Mining Watch partnership (public web platform)
location: Amazon basin (Brazil, Peru, Guyana, Venezuela and other basin countries)
domain: Environmental monitoring: illegal gold mining in tropical forest
segment: Non-profit remote-sensing platform for journalism and conservation
taxonomy_note: Loose fit: the documented output is knowledge (maps and area statistics), not a measured environmental outcome. Technical claims and accuracy figures come from the makers' own repository; the only independent source is one Mongabay news report. MAAP's enforcement-related reports describe no AI role.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an attributable event; no individual beneficiary documented.
General benefit without an attributable event; journalists and NGOs use the maps, but no organization's decision is documented as changed by a detection.
General benefit without an attributable event; basin-wide statistics exist, but no enforcement or policy outcome is attributed to the tool in a fetched source.

ai_role.statement: The AI system produces the maps and area statistics themselves: the makers' repository describes an ensemble of convolutional neural networks on Sentinel-2 patches with reported holdout specificity 0.976 and sensitivity 0.991, and Mongabay independently describes the platform as training AI algorithms to recognize mining scars. No fetched source links a detection to an enforcement action; Mongabay's remark that the platform is useful for cross-border work, citing 2025 Brazil-Colombia operations on the Pure River, does not state that those operations used its detections. MAAP's Operation Mercury analysis (same maker) used satellite imagery without machine learning.
